newsitem.title: USA: S. Carolina jobless rate drops to 5.4 pct in March.
newsitem.headline: S. Carolina jobless rate drops to 5.4 pct in March.

text.p: South Carolina's unemployment rate dropped to 5.3 percent in March from 5.5 percent in February and 5.7 percent a year ago, the Employment Security Commission said Tuesday.
"For the first time in 15 months, the number of unemployed dipped below the 100,000 mark," Executive Director Joel Cassidy said.
All major industry divisions experienced employment gains over the month. Nonfarm employment was up by 19,200, with trade and services accounting for well over 13,000 of those jobs.

Cassidy said warm weather and tourism should continue to brighten job prospects in the coming weeks. However, the summer recess at high schools and colleges will probably swell the labor market with students looking for jobs.
Berkeley and Lexington counties had the state's lowest jobless rate, 2.6 percent, while Williamsburg County had the highest, 17 percent.
